title: Federal court instruments on generative AI in filings
description: Standing orders, local rules, general orders and published guidance of United States federal courts and judges on the use of generative artificial intelligence in court filings. Every entry was compiled from the court's own published text (source_kind primary) and records what the instrument asks of a filer. Facts are not copyrightable; quoted order text is a work of the United States Government. The compilation is released under CC0-1.0.

kind.certification_every_filing: A statement about generative AI is required in every filing, whether or not AI was used.
kind.disclosure_when_used: A disclosure, declaration or certificate is required when generative AI was used.
kind.prohibition: Generative AI may not be used to prepare filings, with stated carve-outs.
kind.verification_only: No disclosure; the filer must verify AI-assisted content and remains responsible for it.
kind.guidance: Advisory text; restates Rule 11 or Rule 9011 duties without a new requirement.

applies_to.attorneys: Counsel only, by the instrument's wording.

elements.tool_name: Name the generative AI program used.
elements.portions: Identify the portions of text drafted with AI.
elements.how_used: Describe how the tool was used.
elements.accuracy_certification: Certify that AI-drafted content was checked for accuracy.
elements.citations_verified: Certify that every citation was verified.
elements.human_review: A human reviewed and approved AI-drafted text.
elements.confidentiality: Certify that no confidential or business proprietary information was disclosed to the tool.
elements.prompt_records: Retain records of prompts submitted to the tool.
elements.negative_certification_when_unused: The filer certifies that no generative AI was used: by filing without the disclosure, or by a statement of non-use that the instrument requires.
elements.signed_by_all_drafters: Everyone who contributed to drafting signs the certification.

caption.placement.first_page_heading: The disclosure appears on the first page under the given heading.
caption.placement.statement_title: The statement or declaration carries the given title.
caption.placement.separate_declaration: Filed as a separate declaration with the given caption.

status.current: Posted and in force on the retrieval date.
status.superseded: Replaced by a later instrument named in superseded_by.
status.rescinded: Withdrawn by the issuing judge or court.
status.inactive: Still posted, but the issuing judge has left the court.
status.proposed: Proposed and pending on the retrieval date.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas

entries.instrument: Local Civil Rule 7.2(f); Local Criminal Rule 47.2(e)
entries.title: Disclosure of Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Effective date. Adopted by Special Order 2-98. Unchanged in the rules effective 2026-09-01.
entries.key_language: A brief prepared using generative artificial intelligence must disclose this fact on the first page under the heading 'Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence.'
entries.notes: Subsection (f)(3): a party who files a brief without the disclosure certifies that no part of the brief was prepared using generative AI. The presiding judge may direct disclosure of the specific parts.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas

entries.title: Mandatory Certification Regarding Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Date first published; the first federal judge-level requirement.
entries.key_language: I further certify that no portion of any filing in this case will be drafted by generative artificial intelligence or that any language drafted by generative artificial intelligence—including quotations, citations, paraphrased assertions, and legal analysis—will be checked for accuracy, using print reporters or traditional legal databases, by a human being before it is submitted to the Court.
entries.notes: The judge's page now states that he no longer requires the certification in light of Local Civil Rule 7.2(f) and Local Criminal Rule 47.2(e). The certificate template remains posted.

court.name: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas

entries.instrument: Local Rule CV-11(g); Local Rule AT-3(m)
entries.title: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technology by Pro Se Litigants
entries.date_note: Effective date of General Order 23-11. Amended by General Order 25-07, effective 2025-12-01, to apply to all litigants.
entries.key_language: CV-11(g) is amended to make clear that its warning and referenced obligations apply to all litigants, represented by counsel and pro se, and all contents of a document.
entries.notes: The 2023 rule was written to alert pro se litigants; the quoted sentence is the court's comment on the 2025 amendment. Litigants remain bound by Rule 11 and must review and verify computer-generated content.

court.name: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas

entries.title: Standing Order on Disclosure and Certification Requirements for Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

caption.text: Certificate of Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage

entries.key_language: any party, whether appearing pro se or through counsel, must include with all filings a 'Certificate of Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage' that discloses: (1) 'generative artificial intelligence' was used (or not used); (2) the specific tool the party used; (3) how the party used the tool
entries.notes: Element (4) is a certification that the party checked the accuracy of the AI-assisted content. Omitting the certificate is deemed a certification of non-use.

court.name: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas

entries.title: Disclosure and Certification Requirements for Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

caption.text: Certificate of Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage

entries.key_language: all parties—represented or appearing pro se in criminal cases and/or civil cases
entries.notes: Restates Rule 11, CV-11(g) and AT-3(m); the certificate includes a statement that no confidential or privileged information was disclosed to the tool.

court.name: United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas

entries.title: In re: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Court Filings
entries.key_language: Attorneys and self-represented litigants are cautioned against submitting to the Court any pleading
entries.notes: The sentence continues: drafted using generative artificial intelligence without checking the submission for accuracy. Signers are responsible under Rule 11; no certificate is required.

court.name: United States District Court for the Western District of Texas

entries.title: Standing Order Concerning the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Preparation of Filings

caption.text: Certificate of Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage

entries.key_language: This document was generated with the assistance of [Name of Program], a generative artificial intelligence tool. I hereby certify that I have independently verified the accuracy of the legal and factual assertions contained in this document
entries.notes: The quoted text is the form in Appendix A. The preamble covers parties represented or appearing pro se in criminal and civil cases.

court.name: United States Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas

entries.title: Pleadings Using Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.key_language: all attorneys and pro se litigants
entries.notes: AI-generated language must be checked for accuracy using print reporters, traditional legal databases or other reliable means; Rule 9011 sanctions apply.

court.name: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania

entries.title: Standing Order Re: Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in Cases Assigned to Judge Baylson
entries.key_language: they MUST, in a clear and plain factual statement, disclose that AI has been used in any way in the preparation of the filing and CERTIFY that each and every citation to the law, or the record in the paper, has been verified as accurate.
entries.notes: Applies to any attorney for a party, or a pro se party. Covers artificial intelligence generally, not only generative AI.

court.name: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania

entries.title: Standing Order Re: Artificial Intelligence in Cases Assigned to Judge Scott
entries.key_language: disclose what specific generative AI program was used, and CERTIFY that each and every citation of legal authority has been verified as accurate.
entries.notes: Triggered when generative AI was used in a citation of any legal authority; applies to any attorney for a party, or a pro se party.

court.name: United States District Court for the Western District of Oklahoma

entries.title: Disclosure and Certification Requirements – Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Date as listed by the Ropes & Gray tracker; the posted document is undated.
entries.key_language: certify in the document that the person has checked the accuracy of any portion of the document drafted by generative AI, including all citations and legal authority.
entries.notes: Applies to any party, whether appearing pro se or through counsel. Failure to disclose and certify may result in sanctions. The same three-paragraph text is used by Judge Kobayashi (D. Haw.) and Judge Strickland (D.N.M.).

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Hawaii

entries.title: Disclosure and Certification Requirements – Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Date of the posted PDF.
entries.key_language: any party, whether appearing pro se or through counsel, who utilizes any generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool in the preparation of any documents to be filed with the Court, must disclose in the document that AI was used
entries.notes: Word-for-word the Palk text.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Hawaii

entries.title: In re: Use of Unverified Sources
entries.key_language: verifies that the counsel or pro se party has confirmed that any such material is not fictitious.
entries.notes: Signed by all four district judges. Unverified sources include briefs generated by AI platforms. No declaration is needed when every source can be located on Westlaw, Lexis or Bloomberg. The posted PDF is a scanned image; text confirmed from the court's quotation in Hoosier v. Executive Centre Ass'n (D. Haw. 2025).

court.name: United States District Court for the District of New Mexico

entries.title: Standing Order Establishing Disclosure and Certification Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Date of the posted PDF; one tracker lists an earlier version from January 2024.
entries.key_language: any party, whether appearing pro se or through counsel
entries.notes: Palk text verbatim.

court.name: United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio

entries.instrument: Standing Order Governing Civil Cases, § VI
entries.title: Artificial Intelligence ("AI") Provision
entries.date_note: Effective date of the current provision; the ban was first effective 2023-07-14.
entries.key_language: No attorney for a party, or a pro se party, may use Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in the preparation of any filing submitted to the Court.
entries.notes: Carve-out for legal search engines such as Westlaw or LexisNexis, Internet search engines, and Microsoft Suite products. Violations may bring striking, economic sanctions, contempt or dismissal. The same provision appears in the judge's criminal standing order.

court.name: United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio

entries.title: Standing Order on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

caption.text: Disclosure of the Use of Generative AI

entries.key_language: any party, including a pro se litigant
entries.notes: The declaration identifies the AI-generated content by page, section or paragraph number and the platform used, and certifies verification.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio

entries.title: Court's Standing Order on the Use of Generative AI
entries.date_note: Date listed by trackers; the posted PDF was created 2023-12-19.
entries.key_language: no attorney for a party, or a pro se party, may use Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in the preparation of any filing submitted to the Court.
entries.notes: Carve-out for Westlaw, Lexis, Google and Bing; duty to inform the Court. Same template as Judge Newman.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of California

entries.instrument: Standing Order for Civil Cases, § H.4
entries.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
entries.date_note: Date the provision was added; current revision 2026-08-26.
entries.key_language: Any submission containing AI-generated content must include a certification that lead trial counsel has personally verified the content's accuracy.
entries.notes: Counsel must keep records of all prompts submitted to generative AI tools. Failure to certify is grounds for sanctions.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Colorado

entries.title: Standing Order Regarding the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in Court Filings
entries.date_note: Effective date.
entries.key_language: Every filing shall contain an AI Certification regarding the use, or non-use, of generative AI (such as ChatGPT, Harvey.AI, or Google Gemini) in preparing the filing, signed by all individuals who contributed to the drafting of the filing.
entries.notes: Example wording supplied by the order: The undersigned counsel certifies/certify that generative artificial intelligence was not used to draft this filing. Non-compliant filings may be stricken with leave to re-file.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Colorado

entries.title: Standing Order Requiring Certification Re: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Filings
entries.date_note: Date of the order ("DATED: October 21, 2024").
entries.key_language: The preparer of the filing must certify either that (a) no portion of the filing was drafted by AI, or that (b) any language drafted by AI (even if later edited by a human being) was personally reviewed by the filer or another human being for accuracy using print reporters or traditional legal databases and attesting that the legal citations are to actual existing cases or cited authority.
entries.notes: Applies in cases where the parties have consented to magistrate judge jurisdiction, and only to motions under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12 or 56, motions to amend a pleading, and any opposed motion with its response and reply. Where the court is in the referral role, it applies only to nondispositive, opposed referred motions. The certification is in addition to the Certification of Conferral. The court will strike a covered filing that lacks it. The order does not prescribe a heading.

court.name: United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida

entries.title: In re: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.key_language: (1) That no generative AI was used… or (2) …that any language drafted by AI—even if later edited by a human—was personally reviewed by the filer or another human for accuracy
entries.notes: The certification goes at the end of every filing by a party through counsel or pro se.

court.name: United States District Court for the Southern District of New York

entries.title: Use of ChatGPT and Other Tools
entries.date_note: Date the provision first appeared; current revision 2026-05-11.
entries.key_language: Use of ChatGPT or other such tools is not prohibited, but counsel must at all times personally confirm for themselves the accuracy of any research conducted by these means.
entries.notes: The judge's separate Individual Practices in Civil Pro Se Cases contain no AI provision.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
entries.key_language: Anyone—counsel and unrepresented parties alike—using AI in connection with the filing… must comply with Rule 11(b) and Rule 26(g).

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois

entries.title: Generative AI disclosure provision
entries.date_note: Date the disclosure requirement was added; withdrawn in the 2024-12-20 revision. Current order dated 2026-03-03.
entries.key_language: The Court will continue to presume that the pre-existing Rule 11 certification is a representation by filers, as living, breathing, thinking human beings, that they themselves have read and analyzed all cited authorities to ensure that such authorities actually exist and that the filings comply with Rule 11(b)(2).
entries.notes: The quoted sentence is from the current order's appendix, which is advisory. The 2023 text required identifying the tool and how it was used; the judge said in August 2024 that the requirement was no longer necessary.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois

entries.title: The Use of "Artificial Intelligence" in the Preparation of Documents Filed Before This Court
entries.key_language: Any party using AI in the preparation of materials submitted to the court must disclose in the filing that an AI tool was used to conduct legal research and/or was used in any way in the preparation of the submitted document.
entries.notes: The order states it is based on Judge Starr's rule. Judge Cole retired on 2025-05-06 and the court's copy was removed; the source is a mirror of the court's PDF.

court.name: United States Court of International Trade

entries.title: Standing Order on the Use of Artificial Intelligence
entries.key_language: (1) A disclosure notice that identifies the program used, the manner in which it was used, and the specific portions of text that have been drafted; (2) A certification that counsel or the party has reviewed the included text and legal research for factual and legal accuracy
entries.notes: Element (3) certifies that no confidential or business proprietary information was disclosed without authorisation. The preamble names counsel and pro se litigants.

court.name: United States Court of International Trade

entries.title: Order on Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Date of the posted order; an earlier version is listed by trackers from March 2024.
entries.key_language: A disclosure notice that identifies the program used and the specific portions of text that have been so drafted

court.name: United States Court of International Trade

entries.title: Order on Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Date of the posted order; an earlier version is listed by trackers from March 2024.
entries.key_language: A certification that the use of such program has not resulted in the disclosure of any confidential or business proprietary information to any unauthorized party

court.name: United States Court of International Trade

entries.title: Order on Artificial Intelligence
entries.key_language: any submission in a case assigned to Judge Vaden that contains text drafted with the assistance of a generative artificial intelligence program on the basis of natural language prompts, including but not limited to ChatGPT and Google Bard, must be accompanied by
entries.notes: Judge Vaden left the court in June 2025; the order remains posted. The template for the Restani, Kelly and Choe-Groves orders.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Nebraska

entries.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: First effective as 7.1(d)(4)(B); amended and renumbered effective 2025-12-01, dropping the earlier certificate options.
entries.key_language: All parties are required, if using generative artificial intelligence programs, to verify the contents of their filings
entries.notes: Unverified filings may be stricken and sanctioned.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Kansas

entries.title: In re: Use of Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in Preparing Court Filings
entries.key_language: reminds and cautions all lawyers and parties, including pro se litigants
entries.notes: The court may strike non-compliant filings sua sponte and may require a sworn statement disclosing AI use, the tool, the portions and the verification done.

court.name: United States District Court for the Western District of North Carolina

entries.title: In re: Use of Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Supersedes the court's 2024-06-18 standing order, which required a separate certificate.
entries.key_language: The requirements of this Order apply equally to attorneys and pro se parties.
entries.notes: Paragraph 7: the filing of a separate certificate regarding the use of AI is no longer required; signing a filing is a certification of human verification.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Wyoming

entries.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Preparation of Filings
entries.key_language: This practice is strictly prohibited and subject to sanction
entries.notes: The quoted sentence refers to citing hallucinated authority, not to AI use itself. A Rule 11 reminder to all litigants, represented or pro se. Scanned PDF.

court.name: United States Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Oklahoma

entries.title: General Order 23-01
entries.date_note: Effective date; signed 2023-07-25.
entries.key_language: any document drafted with generative AI must include an attestation identifying the program and text, certifying accuracy check and no disclosure of confidential information
entries.notes: key_language is a close paraphrase of the order's attestation requirement, not a verbatim sentence.

court.name: United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York

entries.instrument: Local Bankruptcy Rule 9011-1(d), adopted by General Order M-641
entries.title: Generative AI
entries.date_note: Effective date.
entries.key_language: litigants are responsible for the accuracy of technology-assisted documents and must review and verify computer-generated content
entries.notes: key_language is a close paraphrase, not a verbatim sentence. No disclosure requirement.

court.name: United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of California

entries.title: In re: Filings Using Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.date_note: Effective date; signed 2025-11-18.

caption.text: Disclosure and Certification on Generative Artificial Intelligence Use

entries.key_language: any paper prepared in any aspect with generative AI must carry an attestation identifying the program and certifying accuracy check
entries.notes: key_language is a close paraphrase; the signed order is a scanned image. The caption is the title of Local Form CSD 5013. Applies to attorneys and self-represented litigants.

court.name: United States Bankruptcy Appellate Panel of the Tenth Circuit

entries.title: In re: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Submissions
entries.key_language: will issue a Notice and Order striking the pleading
entries.notes: Parties are singularly responsible for verifying the content and veracity of any pleading regardless of AI use; a struck pleading may be corrected within 14 days; Rule 9011 applies.

court.name: United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois

entries.title: Using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in Your Court Case
entries.date_note: Undated page; copyright year 2025.
entries.key_language: Never assume a citation, case, statute, or quote provided by GenAI is real.

court.name: United States District Court for the Middle District of Georgia

entries.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence (Guidance for Pro Se Litigants)
entries.key_language: Pro se parties are strongly encouraged to be cautious when using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT
entries.notes: Warns that Rule 11 sanctions can include dismissal.

court.name: United States District Court for the District of Colorado

entries.title: Standing Order Regarding the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence ("AI") in Court Filings
entries.date_note: Effective date as stated on the face of the order.
entries.key_language: every filing shall contain an AI Certification regarding the use, or non-use, of generative AI (such as ChatGPT, Harvey.AI, or Google Gemini) in preparing the filing, signed by all individuals who contributed to the drafting of the filing.
entries.notes: In consented cases, applies to every filing. In cases where the court is in the referral role, applies only to opposed motions referred to the court. AI Certification does not count against page limits. The court will strike non-compliant filings and may award attorney fees where an AI filing lacked substantial justification.

court.name: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit

entries.instrument: Proposed amendment to 5th Cir. R. 32.3 and Form 6
entries.title: Proposed certification regarding generative artificial intelligence
entries.date_note: Notice date; comments through 2024-01-04; the court declined to adopt the rule in June 2024.
entries.key_language: 'I used AI' will not be an excuse for an otherwise sanctionable offense.
entries.notes: The proposal would have required counsel and unrepresented filers to certify either that no generative AI was used or that all generated text was reviewed for accuracy by a human. The quoted sentence is from the court's June 2024 decision not to adopt it. Proposal text: https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/docs/default-source/default-document-library/public-comment-local-rule-32-3-and-form-6.pdf
